en.L: And Job answered and said:
en.B: Then Job answered:
en.R: Then Job said:

es.L: Y respondió Job y dijo:
es.B: Entonces Job respondió:
es.R: Entonces Job dijo:

fr.L: Et Job répondit et dit :
fr.B: Alors Job répondit :
fr.R: Alors Job a dit :

sw.L: Ndipo Ayubu akajibu, akasema:
sw.B: Kisha Ayubu akajibu:
sw.R: Kisha Ayubu akasema:

vi.L: Gióp đáp lời và nói:
vi.B: Bấy giờ Gióp đáp:
vi.R: Gióp nói:

ko.L: 그러자 욥이 대답하여 말했다.
ko.B: 그러자 욥이 대답했다.
ko.R: 그러자 욥이 말했다.

decisions.choice: Job answers Bildad
decisions.reason: This is Job's reply to Bildad's second speech (chapter 18). As in 3:1-2, 9:1 and 16:1, the words that introduce a speech are prose; the speech itself (19:2-29) is poetry.

decisions.choice: answered (Balanced), said (Readable), without "and said"
decisions.reason: Hebrew introduces speech with two verbs, "answered and said". Literal keeps both; Balanced and Readable say it once, with the same wording at every speech introduction in Job.

source.text: עַד־אָ֭נָה תּוֹגְי֣וּן נַפְשִׁ֑י וּֽתְדַכְּאוּנַ֥נִי בְמִלִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Until when will you torment my soul and crush me with words?

en.L: How long will you torment my soul \q and crush me with words?
en.B: How long will you torment me \q and crush me with your words?
en.R: How long will you keep hurting me? \q How long will you crush me with your words?

es.L: ¿Hasta cuándo {{plural_you:atormentarán|atormentaréis}} mi alma \q y me {{plural_you:quebrantarán|quebrantaréis}} con palabras?
es.B: ¿Hasta cuándo me {{plural_you:atormentarán|atormentaréis}} \q y me {{plural_you:aplastarán|aplastaréis}} con {{plural_you:sus palabras|vuestras palabras}}?
es.R: ¿Hasta cuándo me {{plural_you:seguirán|seguiréis}} haciendo daño? \q ¿Hasta cuándo me {{plural_you:aplastarán|aplastaréis}} con {{plural_you:sus palabras|vuestras palabras}}?

fr.L: Jusqu’à quand tourmenterez-vous mon âme \q et m’écraserez-vous de paroles ?
fr.B: Jusqu’à quand allez-vous me tourmenter \q et m’écraser de vos paroles ?
fr.R: Combien de temps allez-vous encore me faire du mal ? \q Combien de temps allez-vous m’écraser avec vos paroles ?

sw.L: Hata lini mtaitesa nafsi yangu \q na kunisaga kwa maneno?
sw.B: Mpaka lini mtanitesa \q na kuniponda kwa maneno yenu?
sw.R: Mtaendelea kuniumiza mpaka lini? \q Mtaniponda kwa maneno yenu mpaka lini?

vi.L: Cho đến bao giờ các anh còn hành hạ linh hồn tôi \q và nghiền nát tôi bằng lời nói?
vi.B: Các anh còn hành hạ tôi \q và dùng lời lẽ nghiền nát tôi đến bao giờ?
vi.R: Các anh còn làm tôi đau khổ đến bao giờ? \q Các anh còn dùng lời nói để chà đạp tôi đến bao giờ?

ko.L: 그대들은 언제까지 내 영혼을 괴롭히고 \q 말로 나를 짓부수려 하오?
ko.B: 그대들은 언제까지 나를 괴롭히고 \q 그대들의 말로 나를 짓밟으려 하오?
ko.R: 그대들은 언제까지 나를 아프게 하겠소? \q 언제까지 말로 나를 짓밟겠소?

decisions.choice: how long: Job throws Bildad's question back
decisions.reason: Bildad began both his speeches with "How long?" (8:2; 18:2). Job answers with the same words.

decisions.choice: my soul: my whole self
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) means the living person, the self. "Torment my soul" means to torment me.

decisions.choice: crush: grind down, break to pieces
decisions.reason: The verb (daka') is used of crushing something into pieces (6:9; Isaiah 53:5). Words can do what blows do.

decisions.choice: me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "me", since "my soul" here means the whole person (m2).

decisions.choice: plural_you on the verbs and possessives Job addresses to his three friends
decisions.reason: Job answers Bildad, but the Hebrew verbs are plural: he speaks to all three friends, as again in verses 21-22 and 28-29. Spanish marks this with the plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: 하오체 with 그대들 when Job speaks to his friends; the plain style in the lament of verses 7-20 and 23-27
decisions.reason: Job's words to the friends keep the dignified 하오체 used between them; where he describes his suffering and his hope without addressing them, Korean uses the plain style of a poem.

source.text: זֶ֤ה עֶ֣שֶׂר פְּ֭עָמִים תַּכְלִימ֑וּנִי לֹֽא־תֵ֝בֹ֗שׁוּ תַּהְכְּרוּ־לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: These ten times you have insulted me; not you are ashamed [that] you wrong me.

en.L: These ten times you have reproached me; \q you are not ashamed [that] you wrong me.
en.B: Ten times now you have insulted me; \q you wrong me without shame.
en.R: You have insulted me again and again. \q You are not even ashamed of the way you treat me.

es.L: Estas diez veces me {{plural_you:han|habéis}} afrentado; \q no {{plural_you:se avergüenzan|os avergonzáis}} [de] maltratarme.
es.B: Ya diez veces me {{plural_you:han|habéis}} insultado; \q me {{plural_you:agravian|agraviáis}} sin vergüenza.
es.R: Una y otra vez me {{plural_you:han|habéis}} insultado. \q Ni siquiera {{plural_you:les da|os da}} vergüenza cómo me {{plural_you:tratan|tratáis}}.

fr.L: Voilà dix fois que vous m’outragez ; \q vous n’avez pas honte [de] me maltraiter.
fr.B: Dix fois déjà vous m’avez insulté ; \q vous me maltraitez sans aucune honte.
fr.R: Vous m’avez insulté encore et encore. \q Vous n’avez même pas honte de la façon dont vous me traitez.

sw.L: Mara hizi kumi mmenitukana; \q hamwoni haya [kwamba] mnanidhulumu.
sw.B: Mara kumi sasa mmenitukana; \q mnanikosea bila aibu.
sw.R: Mmenitukana tena na tena. \q Hamwoni hata aibu kwa jinsi mnavyonitendea.

vi.L: Đã mười lần này các anh sỉ nhục tôi; \q các anh không biết xấu hổ [mà] ngược đãi tôi.
vi.B: Đã mười lần rồi các anh lăng mạ tôi; \q các anh đối xử tệ với tôi mà chẳng chút ngượng ngùng.
vi.R: Các anh đã sỉ nhục tôi hết lần này đến lần khác. \q Các anh đối xử với tôi như vậy mà chẳng biết xấu hổ.

ko.L: 그대들이 이렇게 열 번이나 나를 모욕하고도, \q 나를 학대하는 것을 부끄러워하지 않소.
ko.B: 그대들이 벌써 열 번이나 나를 모욕하고, \q 부끄러움도 없이 나를 학대하오.
ko.R: 그대들은 나를 모욕하고 또 모욕했소. \q 나를 이렇게 대하면서도 부끄러운 줄을 모르오.

decisions.choice: ten times: again and again
decisions.reason: "Ten times" is a round number for many times (Genesis 31:7; Numbers 14:22).

decisions.choice: wrong me: treat me harshly
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here, and its sense is uncertain. It most likely means to wrong or mistreat someone; others relate it to words for being brazen or being astonished. The parallel with "insult" shows that Job is complaining about harsh treatment.

decisions.choice: again and again
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the round number (m1).

source.text: וְאַף־אָמְנָ֥ם שָׁגִ֑יתִי אִ֝תִּ֗י תָּלִ֥ין מְשׁוּגָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And even truly I have erred, with me lodges my error.

en.L: And even if truly I have erred, \q my error lodges with me.
en.B: Even if it is true that I have gone astray, \q my error is my own concern.
en.R: Even if I really have done something wrong, \q that is my problem, not yours.

es.L: Y aun si de verdad he errado, \q mi error se queda conmigo.
es.B: Aunque fuera verdad que me he desviado, \q mi error es asunto mío.
es.R: Aunque de veras yo haya hecho algo malo, \q ese es mi problema, no {{plural_you:el de ustedes|el vuestro}}.

fr.L: Et même si vraiment j’ai erré, \q mon erreur demeure chez moi.
fr.B: Même s’il était vrai que je me suis égaré, \q mon erreur ne regarde que moi.
fr.R: Même si j’ai vraiment fait quelque chose de mal, \q c’est mon problème, pas le vôtre.

sw.L: Na hata kama kweli nimekosea, \q kosa langu linakaa nami.
sw.B: Hata ikiwa ni kweli kwamba nimepotoka, \q kosa langu ni shauri langu mwenyewe.
sw.R: Hata kama kweli nimekosea kitu, \q hilo ni tatizo langu, si lenu.

vi.L: Và ngay cả nếu tôi thật đã lầm lỗi, \q thì lỗi lầm của tôi lưu lại với tôi.
vi.B: Dù cho thật là tôi đã lầm lạc, \q thì lỗi lầm ấy là việc riêng của tôi.
vi.R: Dù tôi có thật sự làm điều gì sai, \q thì đó là chuyện của tôi, không phải của các anh.

ko.L: 참으로 내가 잘못했다 하더라도, \q 내 허물은 나에게 머무는 것이오.
ko.B: 설령 내가 잘못 길을 갔다는 것이 사실이라 해도, \q 내 허물은 내 일이오.
ko.R: 내가 정말 무슨 잘못을 했다 해도, \q 그것은 내 문제지 그대들 문제가 아니오.

decisions.choice: even if truly: a concession for argument's sake
alternatives: even truly I have erred: a confession
decisions.reason: Job does not confess here; he grants a point for the sake of argument, as the next verses show (verses 5-6).

decisions.choice: erred: gone astray without meaning to
decisions.reason: The verb (shagah) and its noun are used of going astray or sinning unknowingly (6:24; Leviticus 4:13; 5:18). Job says that even if he did something wrong without knowing it, it would not harm the friends.

decisions.choice: lodges with me: stays with me, is my own affair
decisions.reason: The verb means to stay overnight (17:2). An error that "lodges with me" concerns only me: it has done the friends no wrong and gives them no right to accuse.

decisions.choice: my own concern (B), my problem, not yours (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m3).

source.text: אִם־אָ֭מְנָם עָלַ֣י תַּגְדִּ֑ילוּ וְתוֹכִ֥יחוּ עָ֝לַ֗י חֶרְפָּתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: If truly over me you magnify yourselves and argue against me my disgrace,

en.L: If truly you make yourselves great over me \q and argue against me my disgrace,
en.B: If you really want to set yourselves above me \q and use my disgrace as an argument against me,
en.R: You think you are better than I am. \q You use my shame to prove that I am guilty.

es.L: Si de verdad {{plural_you:se engrandecen|os engrandecéis}} contra mí \q y {{plural_you:alegan|alegáis}} contra mí mi deshonra,
es.B: Si de veras {{plural_you:quieren ponerse|queréis poneros}} por encima de mí \q y usar mi deshonra como argumento contra mí,
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes se creen|Vosotros os creéis}} mejores que yo. \q {{plural_you:Usan|Usáis}} mi vergüenza para probar que soy culpable.

fr.L: Si vraiment vous vous grandissez au-dessus de moi \q et plaidez contre moi mon opprobre,
fr.B: Si vous voulez vraiment vous élever au-dessus de moi \q et vous servir de ma honte comme d’un argument contre moi,
fr.R: Vous pensez valoir mieux que moi. \q Vous vous servez de ma honte pour prouver que je suis coupable.

sw.L: Ikiwa kweli mnajikuza juu yangu \q na kunihojia aibu yangu,
sw.B: Ikiwa kweli mnataka kujiinua juu yangu \q na kutumia aibu yangu kama hoja dhidi yangu,
sw.R: Mnadhani ninyi ni bora kuliko mimi. \q Mnatumia aibu yangu kuthibitisha kwamba nina hatia.

vi.L: Nếu thật các anh tự tôn mình lên trên tôi \q và dùng nỗi nhục của tôi để buộc tội tôi,
vi.B: Nếu các anh thật muốn tự đặt mình cao hơn tôi \q và lấy nỗi nhục của tôi làm lý lẽ chống lại tôi,
vi.R: Các anh nghĩ mình hơn tôi. \q Các anh lấy nỗi nhục của tôi để chứng minh tôi có tội.

ko.L: 그대들이 참으로 나보다 스스로를 높이고, \q 나의 수치로 나를 논박하려거든,
ko.B: 그대들이 정말 나보다 높은 자리에 서려 하고, \q 내 수치를 들어 나를 몰아세우려 한다면,
ko.R: 그대들은 자기가 나보다 낫다고 생각하오. \q 내가 당한 수치를 들어 내게 죄가 있다고 증명하려 하오.

decisions.choice: if: a condition completed in verse 6
decisions.reason: The "if" begins a sentence that ends in verse 6: if you want to argue this way, then know that God is the one who has wronged me.

decisions.choice: make yourselves great over me: act superior, look down on me
decisions.reason: The verb means to make great; with "over me" it means to boast or lord it over someone (Psalm 35:26; 38:17).

decisions.choice: argue against me my disgrace: use my disgrace as proof of guilt
decisions.reason: The friends treat Job's suffering and shame as evidence against him (4:7-8; 8:4; 18:5-21).

decisions.choice: You think ... You use
decisions.reason: Readable states the two halves as plain sentences, which verse 6 then answers.

source.text: דְּֽעוּ־אֵ֭פוֹ כִּי־אֱל֣וֹהַּ עִוְּתָ֑נִי וּ֝מְצוּד֗וֹ עָלַ֥י הִקִּֽיף׃

records.literal_gloss: Know then that God has wronged me, and his net around me he has closed.

en.L: Know then that God has put me in the wrong, \q and has closed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} net around me.
en.B: then know that it is God who has wronged me \q and thrown {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} net around me.
en.R: But you should know that God is the one who has wronged me. \q God has caught me in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} net.

es.L: {{plural_you:Sepan|Sabed}} entonces que Dios me ha puesto en el error, \q y ha cerrado {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} red en torno a mí.
es.B: entonces {{plural_you:sepan|sabed}} que es Dios quien me ha agraviado \q y ha echado {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} red sobre mí.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} saber que es Dios quien me ha hecho injusticia. \q Dios me ha atrapado en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} red.

fr.L: Sachez donc que Dieu m’a fait tort, \q et a refermé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} filet autour de moi.
fr.B: sachez alors que c’est Dieu qui m’a fait tort \q et qui a jeté {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} filet sur moi.
fr.R: Mais sachez-le : c’est Dieu qui a été injuste envers moi. \q Dieu m’a pris dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} filet.

sw.L: Jueni basi kwamba Mungu amenipotosha, \q na ameufunga wavu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kunizunguka.
sw.B: basi jueni kwamba ni Mungu aliyenidhulumu \q na kunitupia wavu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Lakini mnapaswa kujua kwamba ni Mungu aliyenitendea isivyo haki. \q Mungu amenikamata kwa wavu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

vi.L: Vậy hãy biết rằng Đức Chúa Trời đã làm cong lý tôi, \q và đã giăng lưới {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bủa quanh tôi.
vi.B: thì hãy biết rằng chính Đức Chúa Trời đã đối xử bất công với tôi \q và quăng lưới {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chụp lấy tôi.
vi.R: Nhưng các anh nên biết rằng chính Đức Chúa Trời đã đối xử bất công với tôi. \q Đức Chúa Trời đã bắt tôi trong lưới của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그렇다면 하나님께서 나를 굽게 하셨고 \q 그분의 그물로 나를 에워싸셨음을 아시오.
ko.B: 하나님께서 나를 억울하게 하시고 \q 그분의 그물을 내게 던지셨음을 알아 두시오.
ko.R: 그러나 알아 두시오. 나를 억울하게 하신 분은 하나님이시오. \q 하나님께서 그분의 그물로 나를 잡으셨소.

decisions.choice: God has wronged me: Bildad's word turned back
decisions.reason: The verb ('avat) means to bend, twist or wrong. Bildad asked, "Does God twist justice?" (8:3), using the same verb. Job answers that God has twisted his case, putting him in the wrong.

decisions.choice: his net: God's net, not one of Job's making
decisions.reason: Bildad said the wicked man walks into a net by his own feet (18:8). Job says it is God who has thrown the net over him.

decisions.choice: Job's charge against God
decisions.reason: Job says plainly that God has treated him unjustly. The book lets him say it; at its end God says Job has spoken rightly of him, unlike the friends (42:7), while also rebuking his words (38:2; 40:8).

decisions.choice: then know
decisions.reason: Balanced completes the sentence begun in verse 5 with "then" (m1 of verse 5); Literal follows the Hebrew order.

source.text: הֵ֤ן אֶצְעַ֣ק חָ֭מָס וְלֹ֣א אֵעָנֶ֑ה אֲ֝שַׁוַּ֗ע וְאֵ֣ין מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, I cry out, Violence! and not I am answered; I cry for help, and there is no justice.

en.L: Look, I cry out, "Violence!" and I am not answered; \q I cry for help, and there is no justice.
en.B: I cry out, "Violence!" but I get no answer; \q I call for help, but there is no justice.
en.R: I shout, "Help! I am being attacked!" but no one answers. \q I call for help, but no one gives me justice.

es.L: Mira, clamo: «¡Violencia!», y no soy respondido; \q pido auxilio, y no hay justicia.
es.B: Grito: «¡Violencia!», pero no recibo respuesta; \q pido ayuda, pero no hay justicia.
es.R: Grito: «¡Socorro! ¡Me atacan!», pero nadie responde. \q Pido ayuda, pero nadie me hace justicia.

fr.L: Voici, je crie : « Violence ! » et on ne me répond pas ; \q j’appelle au secours, et il n’y a pas de justice.
fr.B: Je crie : « Violence ! », mais je n’obtiens pas de réponse ; \q j’appelle à l’aide, mais il n’y a pas de justice.
fr.R: Je crie : « Au secours ! On m’attaque ! », mais personne ne répond. \q J’appelle à l’aide, mais personne ne me rend justice.

sw.L: Tazama, ninalia, "Dhuluma!" wala sijibiwi; \q ninaomba msaada, wala hakuna hukumu ya haki.
sw.B: Ninalia, "Dhuluma!" lakini sipati jibu; \q ninaita msaada, lakini hakuna haki.
sw.R: Ninapiga kelele, "Msaada! Ninashambuliwa!" lakini hakuna anayejibu. \q Ninaita msaada, lakini hakuna anayenitendea haki.

vi.L: Kìa, tôi kêu lên: "Bạo lực!" mà không được đáp lời; \q tôi kêu cứu, mà chẳng có công lý.
vi.B: Tôi kêu lên: "Bạo ngược!" nhưng chẳng được trả lời; \q tôi kêu cứu, nhưng không có công lý.
vi.R: Tôi la lên: "Cứu tôi với! Tôi bị tấn công!" nhưng chẳng ai trả lời. \q Tôi kêu cứu, nhưng không ai xét xử công bằng cho tôi.

ko.L: 보라, 내가 "폭력이다!" 하고 부르짖어도 응답을 받지 못하고, \q 도와 달라고 외쳐도 정의가 없다.
ko.B: 내가 "폭력이다!" 하고 부르짖어도 대답이 없고, \q 도움을 청해도 공의가 없다.
ko.R: 내가 "살려 주시오! 공격을 당하고 있소!" 하고 외쳐도 아무도 대답하지 않는다. \q 도와 달라고 외쳐도 아무도 나를 공정하게 판결해 주지 않는다.

decisions.choice: cry out, "Violence!": call for help against an attacker
decisions.reason: To cry "Violence!" was to call publicly for help when attacked or wronged (Jeremiah 20:8; Habakkuk 1:2).

decisions.choice: justice: a fair hearing and verdict
decisions.reason: The word (mishpat) means justice, a just decision in court. Job wants his case heard (9:32-35; 13:18-19).

decisions.choice: Help! I am being attacked!
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cry means (m1).

source.text: אָרְחִ֣י גָ֭דַר וְלֹ֣א אֶעֱב֑וֹר וְעַ֥ל נְ֝תִיבוֹתַ֗י חֹ֣שֶׁךְ יָשִֽׂים׃

records.literal_gloss: My way he has walled up and not I can pass, and on my paths darkness he sets.

en.L: He has walled up my way, and I cannot pass, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sets darkness on my paths.
en.B: He has walled up my road so that I cannot get through; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has covered my paths with darkness.
en.R: God has blocked my road, so I cannot get past. \q He has made my paths dark.

es.L: Ha cercado mi camino, y no puedo pasar, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pone tinieblas sobre mis senderos.
es.B: Ha cerrado mi camino con un muro para que no pueda pasar; \q ha cubierto de tinieblas mis senderos.
es.R: Dios me ha bloqueado el camino, y no puedo seguir. \q Ha oscurecido mis senderos.

fr.L: Il a muré mon chemin, et je ne puis passer, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} met des ténèbres sur mes sentiers.
fr.B: Il a barré ma route d’un mur pour que je ne puisse pas passer ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a couvert mes sentiers de ténèbres.
fr.R: Dieu a bloqué ma route, je ne peux plus avancer. \q Il a rendu mes chemins obscurs.

sw.L: Ameizingira njia yangu kwa ukuta, wala siwezi kupita, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} ameweka giza juu ya mapito yangu.
sw.B: Ameijengea njia yangu ukuta hata siwezi kupita; \q ameyafunika mapito yangu kwa giza.
sw.R: Mungu ameizuia njia yangu, siwezi kupita. \q Amefanya mapito yangu kuwa giza.

vi.L: Ngài đã xây tường chặn đường tôi, và tôi không thể đi qua, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đặt bóng tối trên các lối tôi đi.
vi.B: Ngài đã xây tường chắn đường tôi khiến tôi không qua được; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phủ bóng tối lên các nẻo đường tôi.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời đã chặn đường tôi, nên tôi không đi qua được. \q Ngài đã làm cho đường tôi đi tối tăm.

ko.L: 그분께서 내 길을 담으로 막으셔서 내가 지나갈 수 없고, \q 내 길들 위에 어둠을 두신다.
ko.B: 그분께서 내 길에 담을 쌓으셔서 내가 지나갈 수 없게 하시고, \q 내 길들을 어둠으로 덮으셨다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 내 길을 막으셔서 나는 더 나아갈 수 없다. \q 그분께서 내 길을 어둡게 하셨다.

decisions.choice: walled up my way: hemmed in by God
decisions.reason: Job said earlier that God hedges him in (3:23). The same picture is used in Lamentations 3:7-9 and Hosea 2:8.

decisions.choice: darkness on my paths: I cannot see where to go
decisions.reason: Darkness on the path means confusion and danger: Job cannot see a way out (12:25; 23:17).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, the subject of verses 6-13.

source.text: כְּ֭בוֹדִי מֵעָלַ֣י הִפְשִׁ֑יט וַ֝יָּ֗סַר עֲטֶ֣רֶת רֹאשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: My honor from upon me he has stripped, and has removed the crown of my head.

en.L: He has stripped my honor from me \q and removed the crown from my head.
en.B: He has stripped me of my honor \q and taken the crown from my head.
en.R: He has taken away my good name. \q He has taken away my place of honor.

es.L: Me ha despojado de mi honra \q y ha quitado la corona de mi cabeza.
es.B: Me ha despojado de mi honor \q y me ha quitado la corona de la cabeza.
es.R: Me ha quitado mi buen nombre. \q Me ha quitado mi lugar de honor.

fr.L: Il m’a dépouillé de ma gloire \q et a ôté la couronne de ma tête.
fr.B: Il m’a dépouillé de mon honneur \q et m’a retiré la couronne de la tête.
fr.R: Il m’a enlevé ma bonne réputation. \q Il m’a enlevé ma place d’honneur.

sw.L: Amenivua heshima yangu \q na kuiondoa taji ya kichwa changu.
sw.B: Amenivua heshima yangu \q na kuniondolea taji kichwani mwangu.
sw.R: Ameniondolea sifa yangu njema. \q Ameniondolea nafasi yangu ya heshima.

vi.L: Ngài đã lột vinh dự khỏi tôi \q và cất mão miện khỏi đầu tôi.
vi.B: Ngài đã tước đoạt danh dự của tôi \q và lấy đi mão miện trên đầu tôi.
vi.R: Ngài đã lấy mất thanh danh của tôi. \q Ngài đã lấy mất địa vị đáng kính của tôi.

ko.L: 그분께서 내 영광을 내게서 벗기시고, \q 내 머리의 면류관을 거두어 가셨다.
ko.B: 그분께서 내 영예를 벗기시고 \q 내 머리에서 면류관을 벗겨 가셨다.
ko.R: 그분께서 내 좋은 이름을 빼앗으셨다. \q 내가 누리던 존귀한 자리를 빼앗으셨다.

decisions.choice: my honor: my dignity and standing
decisions.reason: The word (kavod) means weight, honor or glory. Here it is Job's standing in the community, pictured as a robe stripped off him (29:7-25).

decisions.choice: the crown of my head: my place of honor
decisions.reason: A crown pictures honor and rank (29:14; Lamentations 5:16), not a literal king's crown.

decisions.choice: my good name, my place of honor
alternatives: my honor, the crown of my head
decisions.reason: Readable explains the pictures of the robe and crown (m1, m2).

source.text: יִתְּצֵ֣נִי סָ֭בִיב וָאֵלַ֑ךְ וַיַּסַּ֥ע כָּ֝עֵ֗ץ תִּקְוָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: He tears me down all around, and I am gone; and he has uprooted like a tree my hope.

en.L: He breaks me down on every side, and I am gone, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has uprooted my hope like a tree.
en.B: He tears me down on every side, and I am finished; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has pulled up my hope like a tree.
en.R: He attacks me from every side until I am finished. \q He has pulled up my hope by the roots, like a tree.

es.L: Me derriba por todos lados, y me voy, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha arrancado como un árbol mi esperanza.
es.B: Me derriba por todas partes, y estoy acabado; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha arrancado mi esperanza como a un árbol.
es.R: Me ataca por todos lados hasta acabar conmigo. \q Ha arrancado de raíz mi esperanza, como a un árbol.

fr.L: Il me démolit de toutes parts, et je m’en vais, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a arraché comme un arbre mon espérance.
fr.B: Il me démolit de tous côtés, et c’en est fini de moi ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a déraciné mon espérance comme un arbre.
fr.R: Il m’attaque de tous les côtés jusqu’à ce que je n’en puisse plus. \q Il a arraché mon espoir avec ses racines, comme on arrache un arbre.

sw.L: Ananibomoa pande zote, nami nimekwenda, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} ameling'oa tumaini langu kama mti.
sw.B: Ananibomoa kila upande, nami nimekwisha; \q {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ameling'oa tumaini langu kama mti.
sw.R: Ananishambulia kila upande mpaka nimekwisha. \q Ameling'oa tumaini langu pamoja na mizizi yake, kama mti.

vi.L: Ngài phá đổ tôi tứ phía, và tôi qua đi, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nhổ bật hy vọng tôi như cây.
vi.B: Ngài đánh đổ tôi tứ bề, và tôi tiêu tan; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nhổ hy vọng tôi như nhổ một cái cây.
vi.R: Ngài tấn công tôi từ mọi phía cho đến khi tôi kiệt quệ. \q Ngài đã nhổ tận gốc hy vọng của tôi như nhổ một cái cây.

ko.L: 그분께서 사방으로 나를 허무시니 내가 사라지고, \q 내 소망을 나무처럼 뽑으셨다.
ko.B: 그분께서 사방에서 나를 헐어 버리시니 나는 끝장났고, \q 내 소망을 나무 뽑듯 뽑아 버리셨다.
ko.R: 그분께서 사방에서 나를 치셔서 나는 끝장났다. \q 내 소망을 나무처럼 뿌리째 뽑아 버리셨다.

decisions.choice: tears me down on every side: like a building or wall
decisions.reason: The verb (natats) is used of tearing down a house or wall (Leviticus 14:45; Judges 8:9).

decisions.choice: uprooted like a tree: answering 14:7
decisions.reason: Job said that a tree cut down has hope, for it may sprout again (14:7-9). His hope, though, God has pulled up by the roots.

decisions.choice: I am gone: I am ruined, finished, about to die
decisions.reason: "I go" is used of dying (10:21; 14:20; 16:22).

source.text: וַיַּ֣חַר עָלַ֣י אַפּ֑וֹ וַיַּחְשְׁבֵ֖נִי ל֣וֹ כְצָרָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he has kindled against me his anger, and he counts me to himself as his foes.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kindled {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger against me \q and counts me as one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} foes.
en.B: His anger burns against me; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} counts me among {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies.
en.R: God is angry with me. \q He treats me as if I were {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemy.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha encendido {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira contra mí, \q y me cuenta como [uno de] {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} enemigos.
es.B: Su ira arde contra mí; \q me cuenta entre {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} enemigos.
es.R: Dios está enojado conmigo. \q Me trata como si yo fuera {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enemigo.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a allumé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère contre moi, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me compte comme [l’un de] {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} adversaires.
fr.B: Sa colère s’enflamme contre moi ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me compte parmi {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} ennemis.
fr.R: Dieu est en colère contre moi. \q Il me traite comme si j’étais {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} ennemi.

sw.L: Naye amewasha hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu yangu, \q na kunihesabu kama [mmoja wa] adui {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.B: Hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} inawaka juu yangu; \q ananihesabu kuwa miongoni mwa adui {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.R: Mungu amenikasirikia. \q Ananitendea kana kwamba mimi ni adui {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nhóm cơn giận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghịch cùng tôi, \q và kể tôi như [một trong] các kẻ thù của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bừng cháy nghịch cùng tôi; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} kể tôi vào hàng kẻ thù của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời giận tôi. \q Ngài đối xử với tôi như thể tôi là kẻ thù của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그분께서 나를 향해 진노를 불태우시고, \q 나를 그분의 대적 [가운데 하나]로 여기신다.
ko.B: 그분의 진노가 나를 향해 타오르고, \q 그분께서 나를 원수 가운데 하나로 여기신다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 나에게 화가 나셨다. \q 나를 원수처럼 대하신다.

decisions.choice: kindled his anger: his anger burns
decisions.reason: Hebrew pictures anger as a fire that is lit and burns (32:2; 42:7).

decisions.choice: as his foes: as one of his enemies
decisions.reason: The word is plural, "his foes": Job is counted among God's enemies. Job asked in 13:24, "Why do you count me as your enemy?"

decisions.choice: His anger burns (B), God is angry (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plain English way of speaking about anger (m1).

source.text: יַ֤חַד׀יָ֘בֹ֤אוּ גְדוּדָ֗יו וַיָּסֹ֣לּוּ עָלַ֣י דַּרְכָּ֑ם וַיַּחֲנ֖וּ סָבִ֣יב לְאָהֳלִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Together come his troops, and they cast up against me their way, and they encamp all around my tent.

en.L: His troops come together, \q and they build up their road against me \q and encamp around my tent.
en.B: His troops advance together; \q they build up a siege ramp against me \q and camp all around my tent.
en.R: God sends {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} armies against me. \q They build ramps to attack me \q and camp all around my home.

es.L: Sus tropas vienen juntas, \q y levantan contra mí su camino, \q y acampan alrededor de mi tienda.
es.B: Sus tropas avanzan juntas; \q levantan contra mí una rampa de asedio \q y acampan alrededor de mi tienda.
es.R: Dios envía {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ejércitos contra mí. \q Construyen rampas para atacarme \q y acampan alrededor de mi casa.

fr.L: Ses troupes viennent ensemble, \q et elles élèvent contre moi leur chemin, \q et campent autour de ma tente.
fr.B: Ses troupes avancent ensemble ; \q elles dressent contre moi une rampe de siège \q et campent tout autour de ma tente.
fr.R: Dieu envoie {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} armées contre moi. \q Elles construisent des rampes pour m’attaquer \q et campent tout autour de ma maison.

sw.L: Majeshi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yanakuja pamoja, \q nayo yanajenga njia yao dhidi yangu, \q na kupiga kambi kuizunguka hema yangu.
sw.B: Majeshi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yanasonga mbele pamoja; \q yanajenga boma la kuzingira dhidi yangu \q na kupiga kambi kuizunguka hema yangu.
sw.R: Mungu anatuma majeshi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} dhidi yangu. \q Yanajenga milima ya udongo ili kunishambulia \q na kupiga kambi kuizunguka nyumba yangu.

vi.L: Các đạo quân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cùng kéo đến, \q và đắp đường của chúng nghịch cùng tôi, \q và đóng trại quanh lều tôi.
vi.B: Các đạo quân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cùng tiến đến; \q chúng đắp ụ công thành nghịch cùng tôi \q và đóng trại vây quanh lều tôi.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời sai các đạo quân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến đánh tôi. \q Chúng đắp ụ đất để tấn công tôi \q và đóng trại vây quanh nhà tôi.

ko.L: 그분의 군대가 함께 몰려와서, \q 나를 향해 그들의 길을 쌓아 올리고, \q 내 장막 둘레에 진을 친다.
ko.B: 그분의 군대가 함께 진격해 와서, \q 나를 치려고 공격용 둔덕을 쌓고, \q 내 장막을 빙 둘러 진을 친다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 그분의 군대를 보내어 나를 치게 하신다. \q 그들이 나를 공격하려고 둔덕을 쌓고 \q 내 집을 빙 둘러 진을 친다.

decisions.choice: cast up their way: build a siege ramp
decisions.reason: An army besieging a city built up an earth ramp against its wall (2 Samuel 20:15; Isaiah 37:33). Job pictures God's attack as a siege of a small tent, as if an army besieged a hut.

decisions.choice: troops: raiding bands, armies
decisions.reason: The word (gedud) means a band of raiders or troops (25:3; 29:25).

decisions.choice: God sends his armies
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says that he sends the troops, since they are his.

decisions.choice: a deity_pronoun span on "majeshi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}"
alternatives: no span, as the English has none at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The English "His troops" opens the sentence, so it is capitalised anyway and takes no span. In Swahili the possessive follows the noun in mid-sentence, so it takes the span as every other free possessive for God does.

decisions.choice: a deity_pronoun span on "các đạo quân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}"
alternatives: no span, as the English has none at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: "Ngài" stands in mid-sentence after the noun in Vietnamese, so it takes the span, unlike the sentence-initial English "His".

source.text: אַ֭חַי מֵעָלַ֣י הִרְחִ֑יק וְ֝יֹדְעַ֗י אַךְ־זָ֥רוּ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: My brothers from me he has put far, and my acquaintances surely are estranged from me.

en.L: He has put my brothers far from me, \q and those who know me are wholly estranged from me.
en.B: He has driven my brothers far from me; \q those who knew me have become strangers to me.
en.R: God has made my brothers stay away from me. \q The people who knew me now act like strangers.

es.L: Ha alejado de mí a mis hermanos, \q y los que me conocen se han vuelto del todo extraños para mí.
es.B: Ha apartado de mí a mis hermanos; \q los que me conocían se han vuelto extraños para mí.
es.R: Dios ha hecho que mis hermanos se alejen de mí. \q La gente que me conocía ahora se porta como si no me conociera.

fr.L: Il a éloigné de moi mes frères, \q et ceux qui me connaissent me sont devenus tout à fait étrangers.
fr.B: Il a écarté de moi mes frères ; \q ceux qui me connaissaient sont devenus des étrangers pour moi.
fr.R: Dieu a fait que mes frères se tiennent loin de moi. \q Les gens qui me connaissaient font comme s’ils ne me connaissaient pas.

sw.L: Amewaweka ndugu zangu mbali nami, \q na wanaonijua wamekuwa wageni kabisa kwangu.
sw.B: Amewafukuza ndugu zangu mbali nami; \q walionijua wamekuwa wageni kwangu.
sw.R: Mungu amewafanya ndugu zangu wakae mbali nami. \q Watu walionijua sasa wanajifanya hawanijui.

vi.L: Ngài đã đẩy anh em tôi ra xa tôi, \q và những người quen biết tôi đều trở nên xa lạ với tôi.
vi.B: Ngài đã khiến anh em tôi xa lánh tôi; \q những người quen biết tôi đã trở thành người dưng.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời đã khiến anh em tôi tránh xa tôi. \q Những người quen biết tôi nay làm như người xa lạ.

ko.L: 그분께서 내 형제들을 내게서 멀리 떠나게 하셨고, \q 나를 아는 자들도 정녕 내게 낯선 사람이 되었다.
ko.B: 그분께서 내 형제들을 내게서 멀어지게 하셨고, \q 나를 알던 이들은 낯선 사람이 되었다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 내 형제들이 나를 멀리하게 하셨다. \q 나를 알던 사람들도 이제는 남처럼 행동한다.

decisions.choice: he has put far: God is behind his loneliness
decisions.reason: The subject is still God (verses 6-12). Job sees the desertion of family and friends in verses 13-19 as part of God's attack on him (compare Psalm 88:9, 19).

decisions.choice: brothers: his brothers and close kin
decisions.reason: The word can mean brothers or, more widely, relatives. Next to "those who know me" it means his close family.

decisions.choice: surely estranged: become strangers
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a stranger or outsider (zar), used again in verses 15 and 27.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God (m1).

source.text: חָדְל֥וּ קְרוֹבָ֑י וּֽמְיֻדָּעַ֥י שְׁכֵחֽוּנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Have ceased my relatives, and my intimates have forgotten me.

en.L: My relatives have failed [me], \q and my close friends have forgotten me.
en.B: My relatives have let me down; \q my close friends have forgotten me.
en.R: My relatives have abandoned me. \q My closest friends have forgotten me.

es.L: Mis parientes me han fallado, \q y mis íntimos me han olvidado.
es.B: Mis parientes me han defraudado; \q mis amigos íntimos me han olvidado.
es.R: Mis parientes me han abandonado. \q Mis mejores amigos se han olvidado de mí.

fr.L: Mes proches [m’]ont fait défaut, \q et mes intimes m’ont oublié.
fr.B: Mes proches m’ont laissé tomber ; \q mes amis intimes m’ont oublié.
fr.R: Ma famille m’a abandonné. \q Mes amis les plus proches m’ont oublié.

sw.L: Jamaa zangu wamekoma [kunijia], \q na rafiki zangu wa karibu wamenisahau.
sw.B: Jamaa zangu wameniangusha; \q rafiki zangu wa karibu wamenisahau.
sw.R: Jamaa zangu wameniacha. \q Rafiki zangu wa karibu kabisa wamenisahau.

vi.L: Bà con tôi đã bỏ [tôi], \q và bạn thân tôi đã quên tôi.
vi.B: Bà con tôi đã bỏ rơi tôi; \q bạn bè thân thiết đã quên tôi.
vi.R: Họ hàng tôi đã bỏ tôi. \q Những người bạn thân nhất đã quên tôi.

ko.L: 내 친척들은 [나를] 저버렸고, \q 내 가까운 친구들은 나를 잊었다.
ko.B: 내 친척들은 나를 외면했고, \q 가까운 벗들은 나를 잊었다.
ko.R: 내 친척들은 나를 버렸다. \q 가장 친한 친구들도 나를 잊었다.

decisions.choice: my relatives: those near to me
decisions.reason: The word means those who are near, kinsfolk (Psalm 38:12).

decisions.choice: my intimates: those I know well
decisions.reason: The word means those who are known well, close friends (Psalm 31:12; 55:14).

decisions.choice: have ceased: stopped coming, failed me
decisions.reason: The verb (chadal) means to stop or leave off; they have stopped being family to him.

source.text: גָּ֘רֵ֤י בֵיתִ֣י וְ֭אַמְהֹתַי לְזָ֣ר תַּחְשְׁבֻ֑נִי נָ֝כְרִ֗י הָיִ֥יתִי בְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: The sojourners of my house and my maidservants as a stranger count me; a foreigner I have become in their eyes.

en.L: The guests in my house and my female slaves count me as a stranger; \q I have become a foreigner in their eyes.
en.B: My household guests and my female servants treat me as a stranger; \q I have become a foreigner in their eyes.
en.R: The people who stay in my house and the women who serve me treat me like a stranger. \q They look at me as if I came from another country.

es.L: Los huéspedes de mi casa y mis esclavas me cuentan por extraño; \q he llegado a ser un extranjero a sus ojos.
es.B: Los huéspedes de mi casa y mis siervas me tratan como a un extraño; \q me he vuelto un extranjero a sus ojos.
es.R: La gente que vive en mi casa y las mujeres que me sirven me tratan como a un desconocido. \q Me miran como si yo viniera de otro país.

fr.L: Les hôtes de ma maison et mes esclaves me tiennent pour un intrus ; \q je suis devenu un étranger à leurs yeux.
fr.B: Les hôtes de ma maison et mes servantes me traitent en intrus ; \q je suis devenu un étranger à leurs yeux.
fr.R: Ceux qui vivent chez moi et les femmes qui me servent me traitent comme un inconnu. \q Ils me regardent comme si je venais d’un autre pays.

sw.L: Wageni wa nyumbani mwangu na wajakazi wangu wananihesabu kuwa mgeni; \q nimekuwa mtu wa kabila jingine machoni pao.
sw.B: Wageni wanaokaa nyumbani mwangu na watumishi wangu wa kike wananitendea kama mgeni; \q nimekuwa mtu wa kigeni machoni pao.
sw.R: Watu wanaokaa nyumbani mwangu na wanawake wanaonitumikia wananitendea kama mtu wasiyemjua. \q Wananitazama kana kwamba nimetoka nchi nyingine.

vi.L: Khách trọ trong nhà tôi và các nữ tì của tôi coi tôi như người lạ; \q tôi đã trở thành kẻ ngoại bang trong mắt họ.
vi.B: Khách ở trong nhà tôi và các tớ gái của tôi đối xử với tôi như người lạ; \q tôi đã thành kẻ ngoại bang trong mắt họ.
vi.R: Những người ở trong nhà tôi và các cô đầy tớ đối xử với tôi như người lạ. \q Họ nhìn tôi như thể tôi đến từ nước khác.

ko.L: 내 집에 머무는 자들과 내 여종들이 나를 낯선 사람으로 여기니, \q 내가 그들의 눈에 이방인이 되었다.
ko.B: 내 집에 사는 식객들과 여종들이 나를 낯선 사람처럼 대하니, \q 그들의 눈에 내가 이방인이 되었다.
ko.R: 내 집에 함께 사는 사람들과 나를 시중들던 여자들이 나를 남처럼 대한다. \q 그들은 마치 내가 다른 나라에서 온 사람인 것처럼 나를 본다.

decisions.choice: sojourners of my house: guests or dependents living in his home
decisions.reason: The word means those who live as outsiders in someone's house: guests, or dependents who live under the master's protection (Exodus 3:22).

decisions.choice: maidservants: female slaves of the household
decisions.reason: The word ('amah) means a female slave, owned by the household. Even those who depended on Job now treat him as an outsider.

decisions.choice: a stranger ... a foreigner
decisions.reason: The first word (zar) is an outsider, someone not of the family; the second (nokhri) is a foreigner from another people. Job is shut out of his own home.

decisions.choice: female servants (B), the women who serve me (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "slaves"; Balanced and Readable say "servants", as with the word for a male slave, while m2 states their position.

decisions.choice: "un intrus" for the outsider (zar) and "un étranger" for the foreigner (nokhri)
decisions.reason: French needs two different words for the two Hebrew words (meaning decision m3); "intrus" says that Job is treated as one who does not belong in his own house.

source.text: לְעַבְדִּ֣י קָ֭רָאתִי וְלֹ֣א יַעֲנֶ֑ה בְּמוֹ־פִ֝֗י אֶתְחַנֶּן־לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: To my servant I call, and not he answers; with my mouth I must plead with him.

en.L: I call to my slave, and he does not answer; \q with my own mouth I plead with him.
en.B: I call my servant, but he does not answer, \q though I plead with him with my own mouth.
en.R: When I call my servant, he does not answer me, \q even when I beg him to come.

es.L: Llamo a mi esclavo, y no responde; \q con mi propia boca le suplico.
es.B: Llamo a mi siervo, pero no me responde, \q aunque le suplico con mi propia boca.
es.R: Cuando llamo a mi siervo, no me contesta, \q ni siquiera cuando le ruego que venga.

fr.L: J’appelle mon esclave, et il ne répond pas ; \q de ma propre bouche je le supplie.
fr.B: J’appelle mon serviteur, mais il ne répond pas, \q même quand je le supplie de ma propre bouche.
fr.R: Quand j’appelle mon serviteur, il ne me répond pas, \q même quand je le supplie de venir.

sw.L: Ninamwita mtumwa wangu, wala hajibu; \q kwa kinywa changu mwenyewe ninamsihi.
sw.B: Ninamwita mtumishi wangu, lakini hajibu, \q ingawa ninamsihi kwa kinywa changu mwenyewe.
sw.R: Ninapomwita mtumishi wangu, hanijibu, \q hata ninapomwomba aje.

vi.L: Tôi gọi nô lệ tôi, và nó không trả lời; \q bằng chính miệng mình tôi phải van nài nó.
vi.B: Tôi gọi đầy tớ tôi, nhưng nó không trả lời, \q dù tôi phải mở miệng van xin nó.
vi.R: Khi tôi gọi đầy tớ, nó không trả lời tôi, \q dù tôi năn nỉ nó đến.

ko.L: 내가 내 종을 불러도 그가 대답하지 않으니, \q 내 입으로 그에게 애원해야 한다.
ko.B: 내가 종을 불러도 대답하지 않아서, \q 내 입으로 그에게 사정해야 한다.
ko.R: 내가 종을 불러도 대답하지 않는다. \q 와 달라고 애원해도 대답하지 않는다.

decisions.choice: my servant: a male slave of the household
decisions.reason: The word ('eved) means a slave, one owned by Job. Instead of obeying his master, he ignores him.

decisions.choice: plead: beg for a favor
decisions.reason: The verb (chanan, in this form) means to beg for mercy or favor. The master must beg his own slave (compare 9:15).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "slave"; Balanced and Readable say "servant", while m1 states his position.

source.text: ר֭וּחִֽי זָ֣רָה לְאִשְׁתִּ֑י וְ֝חַנֹּתִ֗י לִבְנֵ֥י בִטְנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: My breath is strange to my wife, and I am loathsome to the sons of my womb.

en.L: My breath is strange to my wife, \q and I am loathsome to the sons of my womb.
en.B: My breath is offensive to my wife; \q I am loathsome to my own brothers.
en.R: My wife cannot stand my breath. \q My own brothers find me disgusting.

es.L: Mi aliento es extraño a mi mujer, \q y soy repugnante a los hijos de mi vientre.
es.B: Mi aliento le resulta repulsivo a mi esposa; \q doy asco a mis propios hermanos.
es.R: Mi esposa no soporta mi aliento. \q Mis propios hermanos sienten asco de mí.

fr.L: Mon haleine est étrangère à ma femme, \q et je suis répugnant pour les fils de mon sein.
fr.B: Mon haleine répugne à ma femme ; \q je dégoûte mes propres frères.
fr.R: Ma femme ne supporte pas mon haleine. \q Mes propres frères me trouvent dégoûtant.

sw.L: Pumzi yangu ni ngeni kwa mke wangu, \q nami ni chukizo kwa wana wa tumbo langu.
sw.B: Pumzi yangu inamchukiza mke wangu; \q ninawachukiza ndugu zangu wa tumbo moja.
sw.R: Mke wangu hawezi kuvumilia pumzi yangu. \q Hata ndugu zangu mwenyewe wananiona kuwa kinyaa.

vi.L: Hơi thở tôi trở nên xa lạ với vợ tôi, \q và tôi ghê tởm đối với các con trai của dạ tôi.
vi.B: Hơi thở tôi làm vợ tôi khó chịu; \q tôi thành ghê tởm đối với chính anh em ruột của tôi.
vi.R: Vợ tôi không chịu nổi hơi thở của tôi. \q Chính anh em ruột cũng thấy tôi ghê tởm.

ko.L: 내 숨결은 내 아내에게 낯설고, \q 나는 내 태의 아들들에게 역겨운 자가 되었다.
ko.B: 내 입김을 아내가 싫어하고, \q 나는 친형제들에게도 역겨운 사람이 되었다.
ko.R: 아내는 내 입김을 견디지 못한다. \q 친형제들도 나를 역겹게 여긴다.

decisions.choice: my breath is strange: offensive, repulsive
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) here is breath, made foul by his sickness. The verb is related to the word for a stranger (verses 13, 15): even his breath makes him a stranger to his wife.

decisions.choice: the sons of my womb: my brothers
decisions.reason: "My womb" is most likely the womb that bore Job, his mother's (as in 3:10), so the "sons of my womb" are his brothers. His own children died (1:18-19). Some take the words as his children or grandchildren.

decisions.choice: I am loathsome
decisions.reason: The verb is spelled like the one in verse 16 ("plead"), but here it is most likely from a different root meaning to be loathsome, matching "strange" in the first line.

decisions.choice: my own brothers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the phrase most likely means (m2).

decisions.choice: "ndugu zangu wa tumbo moja" (my brothers of one womb)
decisions.reason: Swahili "ndugu" can mean any relative; "wa tumbo moja" says they are his full brothers, born of the same mother, which keeps the Hebrew's "womb" (meaning decision m2).

source.text: גַּם־עֲ֭וִילִים מָ֣אֲסוּ בִ֑י אָ֝ק֗וּמָה וַיְדַבְּרוּ־בִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Even young boys despise me; I rise, and they speak against me.

en.L: Even young boys despise me; \q I rise, and they speak against me.
en.B: Even young children despise me; \q when I get up, they mock me.
en.R: Even little children laugh at me. \q When I stand up, they make fun of me.

es.L: Aun los muchachos me desprecian; \q me levanto, y hablan contra mí.
es.B: Hasta los niños pequeños me desprecian; \q cuando me levanto, se burlan de mí.
es.R: Hasta los niños se ríen de mí. \q Cuando me pongo de pie, se burlan de mí.

fr.L: Même les petits garçons me méprisent ; \q je me lève, et ils parlent contre moi.
fr.B: Même les jeunes enfants me méprisent ; \q quand je me lève, ils se moquent de moi.
fr.R: Même les petits enfants rient de moi. \q Quand je me lève, ils se moquent de moi.

sw.L: Hata wavulana wadogo wananidharau; \q ninaondoka, nao wanasema dhidi yangu.
sw.B: Hata watoto wadogo wananidharau; \q ninaposimama, wananidhihaki.
sw.R: Hata watoto wadogo wananicheka. \q Ninaposimama, wananifanyia mzaha.

vi.L: Ngay cả bọn trẻ con cũng khinh tôi; \q tôi đứng dậy, chúng nói nghịch tôi.
vi.B: Ngay cả trẻ nhỏ cũng khinh dể tôi; \q khi tôi đứng dậy, chúng chế giễu tôi.
vi.R: Ngay cả trẻ con cũng cười nhạo tôi. \q Khi tôi đứng lên, chúng chế giễu tôi.

ko.L: 어린 아이들조차 나를 업신여기고, \q 내가 일어나면 나를 거슬러 말한다.
ko.B: 어린아이들까지 나를 업신여기고, \q 내가 일어서면 나를 조롱한다.
ko.R: 어린아이들까지 나를 비웃는다. \q 내가 일어서면 나를 놀려 댄다.

decisions.choice: young boys: small children
decisions.reason: The word ('avilim) means little children (21:11). In a culture where the young stood up to honor the old (29:8), being despised by children was deep humiliation.

decisions.choice: I rise: when I get up
decisions.reason: The verb is in a form that can mean "when" or "if I rise". Getting up may mean getting up to speak or simply standing; either way they jeer.

decisions.choice: mock me (B), make fun of me (R)
decisions.reason: To "speak against" someone here is to jeer at them, as the first line shows.

source.text: תִּֽ֭עֲבוּנִי כָּל־מְתֵ֣י סוֹדִ֑י וְזֶֽה־אָ֝הַ֗בְתִּי נֶהְפְּכוּ־בִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Abhor me all the men of my council, and whom I love have turned against me.

en.L: All the men of my council abhor me, \q and those I love have turned against me.
en.B: All my closest friends detest me; \q those I love have turned against me.
en.R: All my best friends hate me. \q The people I love have turned against me.

es.L: Me abominan todos los hombres de mi consejo, \q y los que amo se han vuelto contra mí.
es.B: Todos mis amigos íntimos me detestan; \q los que amo se han vuelto contra mí.
es.R: Todos mis mejores amigos me odian. \q Las personas que amo se han puesto en mi contra.

fr.L: Tous les hommes de mon conseil m’ont en horreur, \q et ceux que j’aime se sont tournés contre moi.
fr.B: Tous mes amis les plus intimes me détestent ; \q ceux que j’aime se sont retournés contre moi.
fr.R: Tous mes meilleurs amis me haïssent. \q Les gens que j’aime se sont tournés contre moi.

sw.L: Watu wote wa baraza langu wananichukia kabisa, \q na wale niwapendao wamenigeuka.
sw.B: Rafiki zangu wote wa karibu wananichukia; \q wale niwapendao wamegeuka dhidi yangu.
sw.R: Rafiki zangu wote bora wananichukia. \q Watu ninaowapenda wamenigeuka.

vi.L: Tất cả những người trong hội thân tình của tôi ghê tởm tôi, \q và những người tôi yêu thương đã quay lại chống tôi.
vi.B: Mọi bạn bè thân thiết nhất đều ghét bỏ tôi; \q những người tôi yêu mến đã trở mặt với tôi.
vi.R: Tất cả những người bạn thân nhất đều ghét tôi. \q Những người tôi thương đã quay lưng lại với tôi.

ko.L: 나와 의논하던 모든 사람들이 나를 미워하고, \q 내가 사랑하던 이들이 나를 등졌다.
ko.B: 가장 가까운 벗들이 모두 나를 혐오하고, \q 내가 사랑하는 이들이 나에게 등을 돌렸다.
ko.R: 가장 친한 친구들이 모두 나를 미워한다. \q 내가 사랑하는 사람들이 나를 등졌다.

decisions.choice: the men of my council: my intimate friends
decisions.reason: The word (sod) is a circle of close friends who share confidences (Psalm 55:15; Jeremiah 15:17).

decisions.choice: abhor: detest, find disgusting
decisions.reason: The verb (ta'av) is strong: to find something abhorrent (9:31; 30:10).

decisions.choice: my closest friends (B), my best friends (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the phrase means (m1).

source.text: בְּעוֹרִ֣י וּ֭בִבְשָׂרִי דָּבְקָ֣ה עַצְמִ֑י וָ֝אֶתְמַלְּטָ֗ה בְּע֣וֹר שִׁנָּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: To my skin and to my flesh clings my bone, and I have escaped with the skin of my teeth.

en.L: My bone clings to my skin and to my flesh, \q and I have escaped with the skin of my teeth.
en.B: My bones stick to my skin and flesh; \q I have escaped with only the skin of my teeth.
en.R: I am nothing but skin and bones. \q I am barely alive.

es.L: A mi piel y a mi carne se pega mi hueso, \q y he escapado con la piel de mis dientes.
es.B: Mis huesos se pegan a mi piel y a mi carne; \q he escapado solo con la piel de mis dientes.
es.R: No soy más que piel y huesos. \q Apenas sigo con vida.

fr.L: Mon os colle à ma peau et à ma chair, \q et je me suis échappé avec la peau de mes dents.
fr.B: Mes os collent à ma peau et à ma chair ; \q je m’en suis tiré avec la seule peau de mes dents.
fr.R: Je n’ai plus que la peau sur les os. \q Je suis à peine vivant.

sw.L: Mfupa wangu umegandamana na ngozi yangu na nyama yangu, \q nami nimeokoka na ngozi ya meno yangu.
sw.B: Mifupa yangu imeshikamana na ngozi yangu na nyama yangu; \q nimeokoka nikiwa na ngozi ya meno yangu tu.
sw.R: Nimebaki ngozi na mifupa tu. \q Ninaishi kwa shida sana.

vi.L: Xương tôi dính vào da và thịt tôi, \q và tôi thoát được với da của răng tôi.
vi.B: Xương tôi dính chặt vào da thịt; \q tôi thoát nạn chỉ còn lớp da của răng.
vi.R: Tôi chỉ còn da bọc xương. \q Tôi chỉ còn thoi thóp.

ko.L: 내 뼈가 내 살갗과 내 살에 붙었고, \q 나는 내 이의 가죽만 가지고 빠져나왔다.
ko.B: 내 뼈는 살갗과 살에 달라붙었고, \q 나는 내 이의 가죽만 가지고 겨우 살아남았다.
ko.R: 나는 가죽과 뼈만 남았다. \q 겨우 목숨만 붙어 있다.

decisions.choice: my bone clings to my skin: I am wasted away

decisions.choice: Redeemer (go'el): the next of kin who stands up for a family member
decisions.reason: The go'el was the nearest relative, whose duty was to buy back a family member's land (Leviticus 25:25), buy him out of slavery (Leviticus 25:48-49), avenge his death (Numbers 35:19), keep his name alive (Ruth 3-4), and defend the helpless in court (Proverbs 23:10-11; Jeremiah 50:34). Job's own family has abandoned him (verses 13-19), yet he is sure that someone will take up his cause.

decisions.choice: who the Redeemer is: most likely God himself
alternatives: a heavenly defender who pleads Job's case before God
decisions.reason: Job does not name his Redeemer. In verses 26-27 he says he will see God, which suggests that God himself will at last stand up for Job, even though Job feels God is now his attacker (verses 6-12). God is often called Israel's Redeemer (Psalm 19:15; Isaiah 41:14; 47:4). Others think of a heavenly figure distinct from God, like the witness in heaven Job spoke of (16:19-21) or the go-between he longed for (9:33; 33:23). Christian tradition has long heard in this verse the hope of a living Redeemer and of resurrection; the text itself leaves the figure unnamed.

decisions.choice: at the last: in the end, or as the last one
alternatives: as the one who has the last word
decisions.reason: The word ('acharon) means "last". It can mean "at last", in the end, or describe the Redeemer as the last to speak, the one who has the final say in Job's case.

decisions.choice: stand upon the dust: rise to speak in court, on the earth or over Job's grave
decisions.reason: "Stand up" is used of a witness or advocate rising to speak in court (Deuteronomy 19:15-16; Psalm 12:6). "The dust" can be the earth (41:25) or the dust of the grave where Job will lie (7:21; 17:16).

decisions.choice: Redeemer (L, B); the one who will defend me (my Redeemer), will stand up for me (R)
decisions.reason: "Redeemer" keeps the family duty of the go'el (m1) and the link with God as Redeemer (m2). Readable says what the Redeemer will do, "the one who will defend me", keeps the word in brackets, and adds "for me" to show that he stands up in Job's defense (m4).

decisions.choice: he with the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The pronoun follows the most likely reading, that the Redeemer is God (m2); see the footnote for the other view.

decisions.choice: "al término" (L), "en el último momento" (B), "se pondrá en pie"
decisions.reason: The words follow the gloss: "last" may mean "at last" or "as the last one" (meaning decision m3), and "stand" is the advocate rising in court (m4). The Spanish avoids the familiar wording of the older Spanish versions; a reviewer should check the line reads well.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun on "il" for the Redeemer
decisions.reason: As the English (decision r-en-2), the pronoun follows the most likely reading, that the Redeemer is God himself (meaning decision m2); the footnote gives the other view.

decisions.choice: "Mkombozi" with the deity_pronoun span on the free pronoun "yeye"
decisions.reason: "Mkombozi" keeps the family duty of buying back that the go'el carried (meaning decision m1) and the link with God as Redeemer; Readable says "yule atakayenitetea" and keeps "Mkombozi wangu" in brackets, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "tôi" for Job, and "Ngài" with the span for the Redeemer
decisions.reason: Job is speaking to his friends here, not to God, so he says "tôi"; the Redeemer is "Ngài" because the most likely reading is that he is God (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "살아 계신다", "서실", with the honorific and no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Korean has no deity_pronoun spans; the honorific -시- carries the reading that the Redeemer is God (meaning decision m2), as the English span does. If the other view were taken, the honorific would still suit a heavenly defender.

decisions.choice: after my skin has been struck off thus: after my body is destroyed
alternatives: after I awake, he will set me up
after my skin, this (body) is struck off
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very compressed: "and after my skin, they have struck off this". It most likely means "after my skin has been destroyed like this", either by the disease that is eating him now (verse 20; 2:7) or in death. The words have been read in several other ways.

decisions.choice: from my flesh: in my flesh, from within my body
alternatives: without my flesh, apart from my body
decisions.reason: The word "from" can mean "from within" (seeing God from inside his body) or "away from" (seeing God after he has left his body). Verse 27 stresses Job's own eyes, which favors "in my flesh": Job expects to see God as himself, in his body, whether before his death or after it. The other reading is that Job will see God after death, without his body.

decisions.choice: I will see God: face to face
decisions.reason: The verb (chazah) is to see or behold. Job longs to meet God in person and be heard (13:15-16; 23:3-7); at the end of the book he says, "now my eye sees you" (42:5).

decisions.choice: in my flesh (B), with my own body (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the more likely reading (m2); Literal keeps the open "from".

decisions.choice: "depuis ma chair" at Literal
decisions.reason: Like the Hebrew "from", "depuis" leaves open whether Job sees God from within his body or after leaving it (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable follow the more likely reading, "dans ma chair".

decisions.choice: "뵐 것이다", the humble verb for seeing a superior
decisions.reason: Korean uses the humble form for meeting God, which fits Job's longing to come before him (meaning decision m3).

records.literal_gloss: whom I, I will see for myself, and my eyes will see, and not a stranger; are spent my kidneys in my bosom.

en.L: whom I myself will see for myself, \q and my eyes will see, and not a stranger. \q My kidneys are spent within me.
en.B: whom I myself will see on my side, \q whom my own eyes will behold, and not as a stranger. \q My heart faints within me!
en.R: I will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for myself. \q I will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with my own eyes, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not be a stranger to me. \q I long for that day with all my heart.

es.L: a quien yo mismo veré para mí, \q y mis ojos [lo] verán, y no un extraño. \q Mis riñones se consumen dentro de mí.

fr.L: celui que je verrai, moi, pour moi, \q et que mes yeux verront, et non un étranger. \q Mes reins se consument au-dedans de moi.
fr.B: {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que je verrai moi-même à mes côtés, \q que mes propres yeux contempleront, et non comme un étranger. \q Mon cœur défaille au-dedans de moi !
fr.R: Je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} verrai moi-même. \q Je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} verrai de mes propres yeux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne sera pas un étranger pour moi. \q De tout mon cœur, j’attends ce jour-là.

vi.L: Đấng mà chính tôi sẽ thấy cho tôi, \q và mắt tôi sẽ thấy, chứ không phải người lạ. \q Ruột gan tôi hao mòn trong tôi.
vi.B: chính tôi sẽ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đứng về phía tôi, \q chính mắt tôi sẽ nhìn thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, không như một người xa lạ. \q Lòng tôi mòn mỏi khát khao!
vi.R: Chính tôi sẽ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Tôi sẽ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tận mắt, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ không còn xa lạ với tôi. \q Tôi hết lòng mong mỏi ngày đó.

ko.L: 그분을 내가 친히 나를 위하여 뵐 것이요, \q 내 눈이 [그분을] 뵐 것이니, 낯선 이가 아니다. \q 내 콩팥이 내 속에서 쇠약해진다.
ko.B: 내가 친히 내 편이 되신 그분을 뵐 것이요, \q 내 눈으로 그분을 뵐 것이니, 낯선 분으로 뵙지 않을 것이다. \q 내 마음이 속에서 타들어 간다!
ko.R: 내가 직접 그분을 뵐 것이다. \q 내 눈으로 그분을 뵐 것이고, 그분은 나에게 낯선 분이 아닐 것이다. \q 나는 온 마음으로 그날을 간절히 기다린다.

decisions.choice: for myself: for my good, on my side
decisions.reason: The words "for me" can mean that Job will see God himself, or that he will see God on his side, no longer against him. Both senses fit after verse 25.

decisions.choice: not a stranger: God will not be a stranger to Job
alternatives: I, and not another, will see him
decisions.reason: "And not a stranger" can describe God, who will no longer be an outsider or an enemy to Job (verses 13-15 used the same word of Job's family), or it can stress that Job himself, not someone else, will see God.

decisions.choice: my kidneys are spent within me: I long for it with all my heart
decisions.reason: The kidneys stand for the inmost feelings (Psalm 73:21; Proverbs 23:16). To be "spent" or to faint is to long with all one's strength (Psalm 84:3; 119:81).

decisions.choice: my heart (B), with all my heart (R)
decisions.reason: English speaks of the heart, not the kidneys, as the seat of the feelings (m3).

decisions.choice: not as a stranger
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the first reading of m2; the footnote gives the other.

decisions.choice: a deity_pronoun span on the relative "lui que" at Balanced
alternatives: "celui que" with no span, as at Literal
decisions.reason: Balanced opens the line with the pronoun "lui", which refers to God (verse 26), so it takes the setting; Literal says "celui que", which takes none.

decisions.choice: "ruột gan" (bowels and liver) for the kidneys
decisions.reason: Vietnamese speaks of the inmost feelings as "ruột gan", as Hebrew does with the kidneys (meaning decision m3); "thận" would read as a plain organ.

ko.L: 그대들이 "우리가 그를 얼마나 쫓을 것인가!" 하고, \q 일의 뿌리가 내게 있다고 말한다면,
ko.B: 그대들이 "우리가 그를 끝까지 몰아붙이자!" 하며, \q 재앙의 뿌리가 내게 있다고 말한다면,
ko.R: 그대들은 "계속 그를 몰아붙이자!" 하고 말할지도 모르오. \q 내가 스스로 화를 불렀다고 말할지도 모르오.

decisions.choice: if you say: a condition completed in verse 29
decisions.reason: The opening word introduces a condition; verse 29 gives its outcome: then fear the sword.

decisions.choice: in me
decisions.reason: The Leningrad Codex reads "in me": Job reports the friends' claim in his own words. Many Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient translations read "in him", which makes the words a direct quotation of the friends. The meaning is the same: the friends say the cause of Job's suffering is Job himself.

decisions.choice: the root of the matter: the cause of the trouble
decisions.reason: The "root" is the cause or source. The friends say Job's suffering comes from his own sin (4:7-8; 8:4; 11:6).

decisions.choice: how we will pursue him!: the friends' resolve to keep after Job
alternatives: what will we pursue in him?
decisions.reason: The words can be an exclamation, "how we will hound him!", or a question, "what charge will we bring against him?" Either way the friends mean to keep accusing Job.

records.literal_gloss: Be afraid for yourselves of [the] face of [the] sword, for wrath [is the] iniquities of [the] sword, so that you may know [there is] a judgment.

en.L: be afraid for yourselves of the sword, \q for wrath [brings] the punishments of the sword, \q so that you may know [that there is] a judgment.
en.B: be afraid of the sword yourselves, \q for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, \q so that you may know that there is judgment.
en.R: But you should be afraid of the sword yourselves. \q God punishes such wrongs with the sword in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger. \q Then you will know that there is judgment.

es.L: {{plural_you:teman|temed}} por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos la espada, \q porque la ira [trae] los castigos de la espada, \q para que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} [que hay] un juicio.
es.B: {{plural_you:teman|temed}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos la espada, \q porque la ira trae el castigo de la espada, \q para que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} que hay juicio.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos {{plural_you:deberían|deberíais}} temer la espada. \q Dios castiga esas maldades con la espada en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira. \q Entonces {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que hay juicio.

fr.L: craignez pour vous-mêmes l’épée, \q car la colère [amène] les châtiments de l’épée, \q afin que vous sachiez [qu’il y a] un jugement.
fr.B: craignez vous-mêmes l’épée, \q car la colère amène le châtiment de l’épée, \q afin que vous sachiez qu’il y a un jugement.
fr.R: Mais c’est vous qui devriez avoir peur de l’épée. \q Dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère, Dieu punit ces fautes par l’épée. \q Alors vous saurez qu’il y a un jugement.

sw.L: ogopeni upanga kwa ajili yenu wenyewe, \q kwa maana ghadhabu [huleta] adhabu za upanga, \q ili mpate kujua [kwamba kuna] hukumu.
sw.B: ninyi wenyewe uogopeni upanga, \q kwa maana ghadhabu huleta adhabu ya upanga, \q ili mjue kwamba kuna hukumu.
sw.R: Lakini ninyi wenyewe mnapaswa kuuogopa upanga. \q Mungu huadhibu makosa kama hayo kwa upanga katika hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \q Ndipo mtakapojua kwamba kuna hukumu.

vi.L: thì chính các anh hãy sợ gươm, \q vì cơn thịnh nộ [mang lại] những hình phạt của gươm, \q để các anh biết [rằng có] sự phán xét.
vi.B: thì chính các anh hãy sợ lưỡi gươm, \q vì cơn thịnh nộ đem đến hình phạt bằng gươm, \q để các anh biết rằng có sự phán xét.
vi.R: Nhưng chính các anh mới phải sợ lưỡi gươm. \q Đức Chúa Trời dùng gươm trừng phạt những tội như thế trong cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Lúc ấy các anh sẽ biết là có sự phán xét.

ko.L: 그대들 스스로 칼을 두려워하시오. \q 진노는 칼의 형벌을 [가져오니], \q 그대들이 심판이 [있음을] 알게 될 것이오.
ko.B: 그대들 자신이 칼을 두려워해야 하오. \q 진노가 칼의 형벌을 불러오니, \q 그대들은 심판이 있음을 알게 될 것이오.
ko.R: 오히려 그대들이 칼을 두려워해야 하오. \q 하나님께서 진노하셔서 그런 잘못을 칼로 벌하실 것이오. \q 그때 그대들은 심판이 있음을 알게 될 것이오.

decisions.choice: the sword: God's judgment turned on the friends
decisions.reason: Job warns the friends that God will judge them for the way they have spoken about him (13:7-11). At the end of the book God's anger burns against the friends (42:7-8).

decisions.choice: wrath brings the punishments of the sword
alternatives: wrath is (one of) the sins that deserve the sword
decisions.reason: The line is compressed: "for wrath, iniquities of the sword". The word for iniquity can also mean its punishment. It most likely means that God's wrath brings the sword as punishment for such wrongs; it could mean that the friends' angry attacks are themselves crimes deserving the sword.

decisions.choice: that there is judgment
alternatives: that you may know the Almighty (Shaddai)
decisions.reason: The last word is unusual. It is most likely the short word for "that" joined to a word for judgment (din): "that there is judgment". Some read the letters as Shaddai, "the Almighty": "so that you may know the Almighty".

decisions.choice: God punishes such wrongs with the sword in his anger
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one whose wrath punishes (m2).
